episodes.200597: Strong wind gusts accompanied severe thunderstorms. The strongest wind gust was in the Glasgow area with 69 mph.
episodes.200695: An upper level disturbance rotated around a large low over the Gulf States to produce a few severe marine storms off the Southeast Coast.
episodes.201009: Mid level height falls ahead of an approaching trough resulted in the development of scattered convection throughout the day. Given dry low levels and a well mixed boundary layer, DCAPE values were high, and numerous dry to mostly dry microbursts were observed across Utah.
episodes.201011: Mid level height falls ahead of an approaching trough resulted in the development of scattered convection throughout the day. Given dry low levels and a well mixed boundary layer, DCAPE values were high, and multiple dry to mostly dry microbursts were observed across southwest Wyoming.
episodes.201271: On May 10th, instability increased across higher terrain in southwest Idaho ahead of an incoming upper-level trough. This allowed for thunderstorms to develop across southwest Idaho. With a dry boundary layer and inverted-V soundings, thunderstorm wind gusts were the primary hazard associated with the storms.
episodes.201274: On May 11th, afternoon instability increased across southwest Idaho as an upper-level trough moved over the region. This allowed for thunderstorms to develop in the early afternoon. The boundary layer was dry with an inverted-V sounding observed.
episodes.201279: Energy on the western extent of a mid- to upper level low centered over the Lower Mississippi Valley moved into our area during the evening. Although PWATs were well below normal and near the 25th percentile for this time of year, showers with a few embedded thunderstorms developed over portions of the Hill Country which were forecast to propagate into South Texas during the evening hours. These storms allowed for isolated instances of elevated marine thunderstorm winds.
episodes.201565: Severe storms in Flathead and Sanders counties produced hail up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.202146: A stationary front meandering across the area combined with diurnal heating and good upper-level divergence promoted localized flash flooding potential.
episodes.202376: An upper-level trough brought in enough moisture and instability to produce severe thunderstorms mainly across the North-Central Montana plains. Severe wind was the primary hazard with thunderstorms.
episodes.202585: Steep mid level lapse rates along with sufficient instability and deep layer shear ahead of a cold front brought a couple of rounds of showers and thunderstorms to the region. Damaging wind gusts were reported across the Florida panhandle. In addition, a couple of tornadoes were reported in Walton county and Holmes county. Flash flooding also occurred in portions of Bay and Washington counties. Rainfall amounts of 3-9 inches were measured.
episodes.202625: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced strong winds in excess of 34 knots across the area.  In addition, a fair weather waterspout was observed.
episodes.202795: An upper level trough and cold front brought a favorable environment for severe thunderstorms. The main hazard was severe winds with thunderstorms, with a few isolated severe thunderstorms produced severe winds to the North-Central plains.
episodes.202987: Rounds of heavy rainfall producing thunderstorms tracked across portions of interior southeast Georgia, producing a few instances of flash flooding. The heavy rain developed near a stationary boundary associated with a surface low situated across the lower Mississippi Valley. Some of the heaviest rain fell across Candler and Tattnall counties where automated rain gages and CoCoRaHS observers reported a range of 5-8 inches of rain. Specific observed amounts include 8.72 inches at the Metter coop site, 7.94 inches at the Reidsville USGS gage, and 7.79 inches at the RAWS site near Metter.
episodes.202988: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms impacted portions of the Atlantic coastal waters and the coastline. These storms developed in the vicinity of a nearby stationary boundary and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.203189: Low pressure and an associated cold front moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms with high wind gusts to much of western and central Wyoming. The strongest wind occurred west of Highway 120 near Irma Lake where a wind gust of 79 mph was measured. Other notable wind gusts included 75 mph along South Pass near Red Canyon, 70 mph at Farson in Sweetwater County, 66 mph at the Dubois airport, and 62 mph in Powell, WY.
episodes.203331: A round of rain and some storms moved across the area during the afternoon of May 11th. No storms were severe, but some gusty winds caused a limb to break and damage a home.
episodes.203716: A weak shortwave produced thunderstorms over the mountains that strengthened near Custer County. Mainly produced strong winds.
episodes.203733: During the second week of May, a nearby deep-layered trough and additional rainfall over saturated soils produced localized flash flooding from May 7th to the 11th.
episodes.203756: Widespread severe thunderstorms reported on May 10th.
episodes.203788: For the second day in a row severe weather was widespread throughout southeast Idaho.
